Introducing
AT1.

10 kg of thrust from four powerful motors on 8-inch tri-blade props and a one-piece PAHT frame. A compact quad that lifts like a much bigger one and takes serious crashes, built for training and for fun.

Made for flying

Small frame.
Heavy lift.
Built to crash.

AT1, Airolit Training 1, isn't a work drone. It's a compact 332 mm quad that lifts 5 kg, for pilots who want to learn how a heavy-lift drone handles without the size of one, and for anyone who wants to fly something with serious punch. The one-piece frame is built to withstand serious crashes, so training mistakes don't end the session.

01
Training

Learn heavy lift

Practise flying with real payloads, and get used to how weight changes braking, inertia and wind handling, on a frame small enough to carry anywhere.

  • Plenty of thrust in reserve for recovering mistakes
  • One-piece PAHT frame built to take serious crashes
  • 20×20 flight controller and 55 A ESC included, with XT90 power
02
Fun

Power to play with

10 kilos of thrust on a 444 g quad is a lot. Punch-outs, long cruises and big smooth lines are what it's for.

  • 8-inch tri-blade props for grip and fast response
  • Room on board for a camera if you want footage
  • Rail system underneath for batteries and payloads

Flight time

Battery, payload,
flight time.

AT1 runs on a high-power 6S pack. With a 22 Ah high-density pack it flies for close to an hour and a half with nothing on board in ideal conditions. Bigger packs fly longer but weigh more, and so does anything you carry. Move the sliders to see the trade-off.

Battery type

Calculated from bench-test data for the motors on 8 × 4 tri-blades at 6S. Measured data covers 50–100% throttle; 10–40% is modelled from two similar motors that were measured across the whole range, matched to this motor's measured curve. Ideal conditions, cruising at around 10 m/s in still air at sea level, which is about 10% more efficient than hovering. Li-ion and high-density packs are flown down to 3.0 V per cell (empty is 2.6 V), which uses about 95% of the pack; LiPo uses 80%. Assumes about 325 Wh/kg for high-density, 230 Wh/kg for Li-ion and 145 Wh/kg for LiPo. Hovering, wind and hard flying use more power, so expect less in everyday flying.

The frame

One piece.
No loose plates.

Most heavy-lift quads are a stack of flat plates and standoffs. AT1 is a single body in high-strength PAHT, with curved bracing between every arm, so the load from full throttle spreads through the whole frame instead of into a few bolted joints. The same structure soaks up impacts, so it withstands serious crashes.

    Underside

    Rail system.

    Twin rails run along the underside of the frame. Batteries and payloads mount to them, so the same airframe can carry anything from a 5 Ah pack to a 36 Ah pack, or a camera or sensor.

    Batteries

    Any pack size

    Small packs for light, punchy flying and big packs for long sessions all fit the same rails.

    Payloads

    Carry what you need

    Cameras, sensors or test weights mount underneath, keeping the top of the frame clear.

    Power

    Straight to the XT90

    The battery lead plugs into the XT90 housing at the back of the frame.

    AT1 Ultimate

    Explore
    the world.

    The Ultimate version adds a 4K camera and a long-range digital HD video link on the nose, with twin antennas behind it, so you can fly AT1 first-person and record every flight. It also comes with GPS, so if the link drops it can stop or fly itself home.

    Spec sheet.

    ConfigurationQuad X
    Wheelbase332 mm motor to motor (diagonal), 235 mm between adjacent motors
    Frame size270 × 270 mm, about 438 × 438 mm over the props
    Motors4 × powerful brushless motors (5–6S)
    Max thrust10 kg peak (4 × 2.51 kg at full throttle)

    Dry weight444 g without battery
    BatteryHigh-power 6S high-density pack: 5, 10, 16, 22 or 36 Ah

    FrameOne-piece high-strength PAHT
    Power connectorXT90, frame-mounted
    Camera (Ultimate)1/1.3-inch CMOS, 4K/60 and 4K/120 fps, 155° ultra-wide, 10-bit D-Log M

    GPS (Ultimate)Included: return to home on lost link, emergency stop
